grade.rationale: The command structure is readable and the repository build analyzer reported no findings, but argument validation, exception boundaries, unchecked scanner-result assumptions, and tightly coupled dependencies create several meaningful reliability and testability risks. Test coverage is unknown.

summary: The implementation is generally clear, but it can silently accept invalid scan arguments, allow path-resolution exceptions to escape, fail while formatting otherwise valid scanner output, and is difficult to unit-test without invoking the concrete security scanner.

grade.rationale: Core command dispatch and security option parsing are straightforward, but regular scan arguments are parsed inconsistently and malformed scanner results can cause output-time failures.
The methods are reasonably focused and naming is clear, although command parsing is duplicated and scanner construction is embedded in command execution.
Control flow and output are easy to follow, but the permissive scan parsing behavior is not evident from the documented usage.
Security failures are translated into exit codes, but scan path normalization occurs outside the exception boundary and finding rendering assumes nested data is always present.

Injected text writers help command-level testing, but filesystem access, elapsed time, hierarchy discovery, and especially the concrete external security scanner remain hard-coded. Coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Path normalization can throw outside the command's error boundary
findings.description: Path.GetFullPath is evaluated before the try block. Invalid path syntax and other path-resolution failures can therefore escape Run entirely instead of producing the documented CLI-style error message and nonzero return code.
findings.recommendation: Move path normalization and existence validation inside the try block, and classify expected path-related exceptions as usage errors with exit code 2.

findings.title: The scan command silently accepts invalid arguments
findings.description: Scan parsing searches for --by-level and selects the first non-option token as the path without rejecting unknown options or additional positional arguments. For example, a misspelled flag can be ignored while the command reports success, and `quality scan --help` performs a scan rather than displaying help.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit argument parser for scan, recognizing help and --by-level, accepting at most one path, and returning exit code 2 for every unknown or duplicate argument.

findings.title: Finding rendering assumes every result has a complete location
findings.description: Output formatting unconditionally indexes Locations[0] and dereferences Range. A scanner result with no locations or a location without a range causes an exception after the summary has already been written, producing partial output and a generic failure exit.
findings.recommendation: Validate scanner results before rendering or format absent locations safely. If complete locations are a domain invariant, enforce that invariant when findings are constructed and expose a non-null primary location.

findings.title: Security command directly constructs its external scanner
findings.description: RunSecurity creates GitleaksSecurityScanner internally, so tests of parsing, exit-code mapping, and output formatting must invoke or otherwise accommodate the concrete process-backed scanner. This makes failure scenarios slower and harder to exercise deterministically.
findings.recommendation: Inject a security-scanner abstraction or a scanner factory into the command entry point, retaining GitleaksSecurityScanner as the production default.
